name: Hyperliquid Strategies Inc.

profile.description: Hyperliquid Strategies is a digital asset treasury company formed in July 2025 through the combination of Sonnet BioTherapeutics and a SPAC. It holds and stakes HYPE, the native token of the Hyperliquid decentralized perpetual-futures exchange, and trades on Nasdaq [5][9]. It has 9 employees in New York, is led by CEO David Schamis (founding partner of Atlas Merchant Capital) and chaired by former Barclays CEO Bob Diamond [5][6]. Fiscal Q4 2026 (June quarter) staking revenue was $6.3M, and reported net income of $471M came almost entirely from fair-value gains on its HYPE holdings [1][3].

innovation.label: WEAK
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): Since its 2025 formation the company has done one incremental thing: it built a staking program (custodied with Anchorage) that grew revenue from $0.5M in fiscal Q2 to $6.3M in fiscal Q4 2026 [1][3][9]. There are no products or pivots beyond holding a single token. AI Deployment (0/2): No AI products or AI-driven savings. Market Share (0/2): We found no data showing category leadership among digital asset treasuries; the business is a passive holder of an asset it does not control. Product Pipeline (0/2): The only forward plan is buying more HYPE (it filed to raise up to $1B for purchases), with no product pipeline [9]. R&D Intensity (0/1): R&D spending is zero [3].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (1/4): The stated aim is to give U.S. and institutional investors exposure to the Hyperliquid ecosystem by accumulating HYPE per share. That is a financial-vehicle mission with no purpose beyond returns [5][7]. Community Impact (0/2): No charitable or community programs found. Employee Retention (0/2): The company is about one year old with 9 employees, so no retention record exists [5]. Insider Buying (0/2): We found no open-market insider purchase data in the last 12 months.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on only 4 of 7 growth metrics (6 weight units), so the score badly overstates the quality of this business. D/E is 0% (1.0), TTM ROE is 39.7% (1.0 at 2x weight), and the TTM net margin of about 3,359% (1.0) all come from FMP-reported figures driven by mark-to-market gains on HYPE tokens, not operating earnings [3]. TTM operating margin is -60% and operating cash flow is negative [3]. FMP's reported forward PEG of -0.04 scores 0 at 2x weight. Revenue growth YoY, 5-year CAGR, and forward P/E are excluded because the company has no prior-year revenue base and no forward EPS consensus [1][3]. Weighted sum 4.0/6 = 6.7, rounded to 7. Liquidity is high at about 19.6M shares/day x $11.01 (~$215M daily).

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (6/9): A token treasury's value depends on HYPE's price and on demand for Hyperliquid's on-chain perpetuals, not on services AI could replace, and AI trading agents could even add on-chain volume. Analysts do not flag AI substitution for the company [6]. The protection is real but not structural like physical infrastructure, because the underlying exchange competes with dYdX, Lighter, and centralized venues, and AI-driven trading tools could shift where liquidity goes [6]. AI Opportunity (0/1): No AI revenue.

infinite_game.summary: Through Sinek's lens, Hyperliquid Strategies is a finite construct: a one-year-old, nine-person listed wrapper built to accumulate a single crypto token and trade at a premium to its holdings. It has no Just Cause beyond token-per-share accretion, no record of courageous long-term choices, and no history in which to show existential flexibility. The experienced leadership team gives it some stability but not an infinite mindset.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (0/3): The company exists to accumulate HYPE and provide public-market exposure to it, with value measured as HYPE per share [5][7]. Schamis's case for Hyperliquid (transparent, self-custodied perpetuals after the lessons of 2008) is an investment thesis, not a cause the company itself advances [6].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): The nine-person team is led by finance veterans with long careers at Merrill, Lehman, Barclays and Atlas Merchant Capital, which gives adequate stability [6]. There is no track record or employee data to show a high-trust culture.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Competitive commentary concerns the underlying protocol versus dYdX and Lighter, and HYPE versus Wall Street exchanges (Hyperliquid's policy arm opposed CME and ICE petitions to the CFTC), an adversarial framing rather than learning from rivals [6][8].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (0/2): The company is too young to have faced a strategic test, and its charter ties it to one token, which by design rules out a pivot. The only 'transformation' was the reverse merger that turned Sonnet BioTherapeutics into a crypto treasury, a financial-engineering event rather than a cause-driven pivot [9].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (0/2): Capital allocation so far consists of raising equity (including a filed $1B raise) to buy more HYPE. We found no examples of giving up near-term results for long-term capability [9].

investment_thesis: The bull case rests entirely on HYPE. Hyperliquid has been described as the dominant on-chain derivatives venue with strong H1 2026 fee generation, and PURR offers regulated, staked exposure to it [4]. The company has no debt, a 41.6x current ratio, a price-to-book of about 1.18x, and staking revenue that grew to $6.3M in fiscal Q4 2026, beating estimates [1][3].
thesis_continued: The bear case is that this is a leveraged-sentiment proxy for one token, not an operating business. Reported profits ($471M in fiscal Q4 after a -$304M loss in fiscal Q2) swing with HYPE's price, operating cash flow is negative, and 92% of total assets are intangible crypto holdings [1][3]. The underlying protocol has faced controversies (the JELLY oracle override and alleged XPL futures manipulation claims), and the shares fell 10.4% in the latest session. A crypto drawdown or a regulatory move against Hyperliquid would hit equity value directly, and new equity issuance to buy HYPE could dilute holders below NAV [8][5].
key_catalysts: Continued growth in Hyperliquid protocol fees and HYPE price appreciation would lift NAV per share directly [4]
Expansion of staking revenue beyond the $6.3M fiscal Q4 2026 run rate as holdings grow [1]
Use of the filed $1B capital raise to buy HYPE at a premium-to-NAV share price, which is accretive per share [9]
key_risks: Single-asset concentration: virtually all equity value depends on HYPE, and fiscal Q2 2026 showed a $304M quarterly loss when the token fell [3]
Protocol and regulatory risk: Hyperliquid has faced manipulation allegations and Wall Street exchanges have petitioned the CFTC to regulate it [8]
Dilution and discount to NAV: digital asset treasuries that trade below NAV cannot issue accretively, and the filed $1B raise could dilute holders [9]
